ess-beta-metadata.label: Modelled unemployment rate
ess-beta-metadata.subtitle: Modelled percentage of economically active people aged 16 years and over without a job and actively seeking work
ess-beta-metadata.longDescription: This indicator shows model-based estimates for the percentage of economically active people aged 16 years and over without a job who have been actively seeking work within the last four weeks and are available to start work within the next two weeks, in Great Britain, for annual periods from January to December, 2004 to 2023.
ess-beta-metadata.caveats:
Unemployment rates are calculated as a percentage of aged 16 years and over economically active population.

As unemployed form a small percentage of the population, the Annual Population Survey (APS) unemployment estimates within local authorities are based on very small samples so for many areas are unreliable. To overcome this model-based estimates have been developed that provide better estimates of total unemployed for local authorities.

These estimates are derived from the Labour Force Survey (LFS) and Annual Population Survey (APS), which have moved from [Official Statistics in Development](https://osr.statisticsauthority.gov.uk/who-we-are/policies/official-statistics-policies/official-statistics-in-development/) to [Official Statistics](https://osr.statisticsauthority.gov.uk/who-we-are/policies/official-statistics-policies/official-statistics-policy/). Since late 2023, ONS has introduced improvements to survey collection, sampling and weighting methods, helping to improve response levels and data quality. Further information on the strengths, limitations and appropriate uses of these data is available in the [Labour Force Survey quality and methodology information (QMI)](https://www.ons.gov.uk/employmentandlabourmarket/peopleinwork/employmentandemployeetypes/methodologies/labourforcesurveylfsqmi).

Updates to this indicator have been temporarily suspended until the APS reweighting is implemented in 2027.

The model-based estimate improves on the APS estimate by borrowing strength from the claimant count to produce an estimate that is more precise i.e. has a smaller confidence interval. The claimant count is not itself a measure of unemployment but is strongly correlated with unemployment, and, as it is an administrative count, is known without sampling error. The gain in precision is greatest for areas with smaller sample sizes.

Refer to the [user guide (pdf)](https://www.ons.gov.uk/file?uri=/employmentandlabourmarket/peopleinwork/employmentandemployeetypes/methodologies/subnationallabourmarket/modelbasedestimatesunemploymenttcm77252969.pdf) for further details.
